 Are we saying that men can receive funding for vasectomy care, however, women who have been sexually abused by men who have NOT had vasectomy care should be disallowed from speaking with a physician about abortion or obtaining one?      Are we inferring that the increased number of men in the military who have received vasectomies  can sleep well at night if they choose to engage in sexual abuse of women in the military because they can't impregnate the female and therefore, she won't NEED an abortion?   From 2018 to 2022, a total of 96,617 men in the Military Health System received vasectomies, with a recent study by military.com showing a trend of younger, more junior, and active-duty service members undergoing the procedure following the Dobbs decision in June 2022. The largest proportion of these procedures were performed on White, married men aged 30-39, with the Army service members receiving the highest percentage of vasectomies.    
Key Statistics
Total procedures (2018-2022): 96,617 vasectomies were performed. 
Age: The 30-39 age group accounted for the majority of vasectomies (53.97%). 
Service Branch: The Army had the highest percentage (36.58%), followed by the Air Force (28%), Navy (21%), and Marine Corps (9.5%). 
Marital Status: A significant 85.37% of men receiving vasectomies were married. 
Rank: Senior enlisted ranks accounted for a majority of vasectomies (64.11%). 
Recent Trends 
A significant shift occurred after the Dobbs decision in June 2022, with a subsequent study from military.com observing an increase in younger, more junior, and active-duty service members seeking vasectomies.
Other Findings
Coverage:
Vasectomies are covered by TRICARE, the military's health insurance, as part of a healthcare model that includes comprehensive reproductive health services. 
Purpose:
Vasectomies are a method of contraception that can prevent unintended pregnancies.
